extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: PIQA (Physical Interaction: Question Answering) is a benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning in natural language. It consists of multiple-choice question answering examples with a goal and two possible solutions, where exactly one solution is correct, and is designed to evaluate models' knowledge of everyday physical interactions and affordances.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk; Rowan Zellers; Ronan Le Bras; Jianfeng Gao; Yejin Choi
extraction.citeAs: Yonatan Bisk; Rowan Zellers; Ronan Le Bras; Jianfeng Gao; Yejin Choi. PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language. 2020.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by prompting annotators with links to instructables.com and asking them to construct goal-solution pairs inspired by the instructions, including a valid solution and an invalid permutation; annotators were seeded with instructables from six categories, data was collected in batches of several thousand triples, and low-agreement examples were removed during validation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Links to instructables.com were used as prompts; the instructables website is described as a crowdsourced collection of instructions for tasks such as cooking, car repair, building, crafting, baking, or manipulating objects using everyday materials.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com, asked to glance at an instructable and construct two component tasks by articulating a physical goal and a valid solution, then provide a permutation of their own solution that makes it invalid; additional qualification HITs were run before collection and validation was performed afterwards by other annotators, with low-agreement examples removed and users with low agreement de-qualified.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data; human performance was calculated by a majority vote.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Reporting bias swamped the dataset in initial unconstrained prompts, with annotators drawn to prototypical solutions and tools in the kitchen or garage and rarely considering other everyday household objects; undesirable annotation artifacts and trivial examples were present and addressed with AFLite
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Some development-set "mistakes" are actually correct but required a web-search to verify; examples with low agreement were removed during validation, including correct examples requiring expert-level domain knowledge that should not fall under "commonsense"; learning about the world from language alone is limiting
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors position physical commonsense knowledge as critical for day-to-day human life and hypothesize it is important for AI systems and robots that interact with the world and understand natural language; they aim to enable construction of language models useful beyond the NLP community, including helping bootstrap robotic-language applications
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding; evaluating and studying physical commonsense understanding in natural language models; probing the inner workings of deep pretrained language models and determining the extent of their physical knowledge; providing a benchmark for progress toward language representations that capture physical knowledge useful for robotic-language applications
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is further cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm introduced in (Sakaguchi et al. 2020; Sap et al. 2019) which is an improvement on adversarial filtering (Zellers et al. 2018; Zellers et al. 2019b). During validation, examples with low agreement were removed from the data.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We compute edit distance over tokenized and lowercased strings with punctuation removed.
